A-OTHER_SPECIFICATION-oral_liquid: One oral liquid event in the evidence involved a release specification other than potency or dissolution: Safecor Health recalled a Vitamin B-Complex, Vitamin C and Folic Acid oral liquid after black particles were observed in the liquid, a Class II event [E5]. The other oral liquid events fail on excluded specifications: Bio-pharm recalled an acetaminophen oral suspension as superpotent after assay failure at the 6-month time point [E3], and Pfizer recalled Quillivant XR extended-release oral suspension for dissolution [E2]. The remaining evidence items are dissolution failures in non-liquid forms [E1][E4][E6][E7][E8][E9][E10].
A-STABILITY_EXPIRY-topical: One topical event in the evidence was driven by stability data that did not support the assigned shelf life: Private Label Partners recalled Selenium Sulfide 2.25% Shampoo, cited as CGMP deviations because stability data did not support the expiry date, a Class II event [E7]. HTO Nevada dba Kirkman recalled lidocaine sprays and creams for the same reason [E8], which are topical preparations. Axcentria recalled Major Oral Peroxide because carbamide peroxide degrades below acceptable levels within the printed 24-month expiry [E2], and Estee Lauder recalled a fluoride toothpaste [E6]; both are oral rather than topical. The remaining items concern powders, injectables or tablets [E1][E3][E4][E5][E9][E10].
A-STORAGE_DISTRIBUTION-sterile_injectabl: Several sterile injectable events involved storage outside permitted conditions. Cardinal Health recalled Wegovy that was removed from refrigerated storage for an extended period and inappropriately released [E3], and Trulicity and Humalog exposed to temperatures outside labelled conditions during inclement weather [E6]. McKesson recalled Infuvite Adult and medroxyprogesterone acetate injection after severe thunderstorms delayed cold-chain transit beyond the specified 48 hours [E4]. Cardinal Health dba Specialty Pharmaceutical Services recalled Nucala prefilled syringes stored and shipped outside labelled storage requirements [E9]. Edge Pharma recalled Methacholine Challenge syringe kits labelled with room-temperature rather than the correct refrigerated storage conditions [E1]. Noven recalled Minivelle after prolonged exposure outside labelled storage, though this is a transdermal system rather than an injectable [E10]. The remaining items concern sterility assurance, not storage [E2][E5][E7][E8].
B-CONTAINER_CLOSURE_DEVICE-ClassIII: Four evidence items are Class III recalls driven by container closure or delivery device failure. United Therapeutics recalled the Tyvaso Inhalation System after water ingress through the lower water cup sensor of the device [E3]. Ascend Therapeutics recalled EstroGel whose pump head detached from the canister unit on removal of the overcap [E7]. Watson Laboratories recalled hydrocodone bitartrate and acetaminophen tablets in bottles whose tamper-evident seals may not have been properly seated [E8]. Apothecus recalled VCF Vaginal Contraceptive Foam whose canister exhibited propellant leakage or loss [E9]. Geritrex was also Class III but was cited as a CGMP deviation for poor closure of a bulk storage container [E2]. The remaining container and delivery-device events were classified Class II [E1][E4][E5][E6][E10].
